meta.title: Learners: Characteristics & Needs
meta.randomizationRule: Randomize question selection/order and answer-option order on every attempt; never reuse an exact attempt signature.
meta.alignment: TKT Module 1 — Background to language learning: differences between L1/L2 learning, learner characteristics and learner needs

questions.prompt: Which learner characteristic is most directly related to differences in attention span, self-consciousness and ability to control behaviour?
questions.correctAnswer: Age and maturity
questions.explanation: Age and maturity can affect attention, behaviour, risk-taking and how learners respond to classroom activities.

questions.prompt: Young learners may often benefit from shorter, varied activities. Which characteristic is this most closely related to?
questions.correctAnswer: Age and maturity
questions.explanation: Younger learners may have different concentration spans and developmental needs from older learners.

questions.prompt: Which factor may make some teenagers especially sensitive about speaking in front of the whole class?
questions.correctAnswer: Self-consciousness linked to maturity
questions.explanation: Adolescents may be particularly sensitive to peer judgement and making mistakes publicly.

questions.prompt: Adults can sometimes bring useful life and professional experience into language tasks. Which characteristic is most relevant?
questions.correctAnswer: Maturity
questions.explanation: Maturity and life experience can influence how learners approach content and classroom tasks.

questions.prompt: Which statement about age is most accurate?
options: Different age groups may need different activity types and classroom support
One age group always learns languages better in every respect
questions.correctAnswer: Different age groups may need different activity types and classroom support
questions.explanation: Age can affect attention, interests, cognitive development, confidence and preferred activity types.

questions.prompt: A teacher replaces a 30-minute teacher-fronted explanation with several short tasks for a class of young learners. What characteristic is the teacher mainly responding to?
questions.correctAnswer: Age and maturity
questions.explanation: The teacher is adapting the lesson to learners' likely developmental and concentration needs.

questions.prompt: Which feature is more likely to differ between children, teenagers and adults?
options: Attitude to risk-taking and making mistakes
questions.correctAnswer: Attitude to risk-taking and making mistakes
questions.explanation: Learners of different ages and maturity levels may differ in confidence, risk-taking and self-consciousness.

questions.prompt: Which teacher decision best shows awareness of learner maturity?
options: Choosing tasks that match learners' cognitive and social development
Using identical tasks for all ages because age is irrelevant
Choosing activities only by textbook page number
questions.correctAnswer: Choosing tasks that match learners' cognitive and social development
questions.explanation: Maturity affects what kinds of demands and interaction patterns are appropriate.

questions.prompt: A class of adults responds well to discussing workplace decisions and real-life problems. Which factor may help explain this?
questions.correctAnswer: Their maturity and life experience
questions.explanation: Adults can often draw on wider personal and professional experience.

questions.prompt: Which statement should a TKT candidate avoid?
options: All learners of the same age have identical characteristics
Maturity can affect attitudes to learning
questions.correctAnswer: All learners of the same age have identical characteristics
questions.explanation: Age is one factor, but individuals within the same age group still differ considerably.

questions.prompt: A child acquires an L1 through everyday family interaction, while an adult studies an L2 for two hours a week in class. Which difference is most relevant?
questions.correctAnswer: Context of learning
questions.explanation: L1 and L2 learning can differ greatly in amount of exposure, purpose and learning environment.

questions.prompt: Which is a common difference between L1 and classroom L2 learning?
questions.correctAnswer: Amount and type of exposure
questions.explanation: L1 learners often receive extensive natural exposure, while classroom L2 exposure may be more limited.

questions.prompt: An adult L2 learner consciously studies grammar rules, whereas a young L1 learner may develop grammar without explicit explanation. Which difference is illustrated?
questions.correctAnswer: Ways of learning
questions.explanation: L1 and L2 learning can differ in the degree of conscious study and explicit instruction.

questions.prompt: Why can the context of L2 learning affect teaching choices?
options: Learners may have limited exposure outside class and need classroom opportunities to use language
Context removes the need for interaction
questions.correctAnswer: Learners may have limited exposure outside class and need classroom opportunities to use language
questions.explanation: Teachers often need to compensate for limited natural exposure by creating meaningful input and use.

questions.prompt: Which statement about L1 and L2 learning is most accurate?
options: They can differ in age, context and ways of learning
They are identical processes in every respect
L2 learning never involves natural acquisition
questions.correctAnswer: They can differ in age, context and ways of learning
questions.explanation: Cambridge explicitly identifies age, context and ways of learning as important differences.

questions.prompt: A learner studies English mainly in a classroom and rarely encounters it elsewhere. Which factor is especially important?
questions.correctAnswer: Context of learning
questions.explanation: The learner's environment limits natural exposure and may affect teaching decisions.

questions.prompt: Which situation most clearly shows a difference in learning context?
options: One learner uses English daily at work; another uses it only in a weekly lesson
questions.correctAnswer: One learner uses English daily at work; another uses it only in a weekly lesson
questions.explanation: The amount and purpose of English use outside class are contextual differences.

questions.prompt: Why might an L2 teacher deliberately create information-gap tasks?
options: To provide interaction that may be less available outside class
questions.correctAnswer: To provide interaction that may be less available outside class
questions.explanation: Classroom tasks can create communicative opportunities that learners may lack in their wider environment.

questions.prompt: Which difference is most clearly about ways of learning rather than context?
options: An adult consciously analyses grammar rules
A learner has two lessons a week
questions.correctAnswer: An adult consciously analyses grammar rules
questions.explanation: Conscious analysis is a learning process, while place and lesson frequency are contextual factors.

questions.prompt: Which conclusion is most appropriate for teaching?
options: Teachers should consider how much exposure and use learners get beyond the classroom
All L2 learners should be taught exactly like young L1 learners
Classroom context has no effect on learning
questions.correctAnswer: Teachers should consider how much exposure and use learners get beyond the classroom
questions.explanation: Teaching choices should respond to the opportunities and limitations of the learner's actual context.

questions.prompt: A learner says diagrams and written examples help her understand new language. What does this describe?
questions.correctAnswer: A learning preference
questions.explanation: A learning preference is a way of learning that a learner tends to find helpful or comfortable.

questions.prompt: A learner prefers to hear a model before trying a new phrase. Which concept is most relevant?
questions.correctAnswer: Learning preference
questions.explanation: Learners can differ in the ways they prefer to encounter or practise language.

questions.prompt: Which teaching response best caters for different learning preferences?
options: Use a reasonable variety of activity types and modes
Label each learner permanently as one type and never vary tasks
Use only the teacher's own preferred method
questions.correctAnswer: Use a reasonable variety of activity types and modes
questions.explanation: Variety can give learners different routes into the same content without treating preferences as fixed limitations.

questions.prompt: Which statement about learning preferences is most useful for teachers?
options: They can influence how comfortable or engaged learners feel with activities
They determine what a learner is capable of learning
questions.correctAnswer: They can influence how comfortable or engaged learners feel with activities
questions.explanation: Preferences can affect engagement, but they should not be treated as fixed measures of ability.

questions.prompt: Why is it unhelpful to treat a preference as a permanent limitation?
options: Learners can use and develop a range of ways of learning
A preference is a medical diagnosis
questions.correctAnswer: Learners can use and develop a range of ways of learning
questions.explanation: Preferences describe tendencies, not fixed boundaries on learning.

questions.prompt: A learner enjoys role play and learns well through active participation. Which learner characteristic is most directly involved?
questions.correctAnswer: Learning preference
questions.explanation: The example describes a preferred way of participating in learning.

questions.prompt: Which lesson plan best acknowledges different learning preferences?
options: It combines examples, discussion, short written work and active practice where appropriate
It uses only one activity type throughout every lesson
It permanently separates learners by supposed type
questions.correctAnswer: It combines examples, discussion, short written work and active practice where appropriate
questions.explanation: A varied lesson can provide multiple ways to engage with content.

questions.prompt: Which statement should a TKT candidate choose?
options: Learning preferences may affect how learners respond to activities
A visual preference means a learner cannot learn through listening
Learning preferences are identical to language level
questions.correctAnswer: Learning preferences may affect how learners respond to activities
questions.explanation: Preferences can influence engagement and response, but they do not define absolute ability.

questions.prompt: A teacher notices some learners like individual reflection while others prefer collaborative discussion. What is the teacher observing?
questions.correctAnswer: Different learning preferences
questions.explanation: Learners may prefer different interaction patterns and modes of working.

questions.prompt: What is the best pedagogic implication of learning preferences?
options: Offer variety while still helping learners develop flexibility
Teach each learner only through one preferred mode
Ignore all learner reactions to activities
questions.correctAnswer: Offer variety while still helping learners develop flexibility
questions.explanation: Good teaching responds to preferences without restricting learners to them.

questions.prompt: A learner writes new vocabulary in a notebook and reviews it regularly. What is this?
questions.correctAnswer: A learning strategy
questions.explanation: A learning strategy is a deliberate action a learner uses to support learning.

questions.prompt: Which example is a learning strategy?
options: Guessing the meaning of a word from context
questions.correctAnswer: Guessing the meaning of a word from context
questions.explanation: The learner is using a purposeful technique to solve a learning problem.

questions.prompt: A learner checks understanding by asking, “Do I really know how to use this?” Which strategy is this closest to?
questions.correctAnswer: Self-monitoring
questions.explanation: The learner is monitoring their own knowledge and performance.

questions.prompt: How can teachers help learners develop learning strategies?
options: Model useful strategies and give learners chances to practise them
Tell learners there is only one correct strategy
questions.correctAnswer: Model useful strategies and give learners chances to practise them
questions.explanation: Strategies can be made explicit and practised so learners become more independent.

questions.prompt: Which strategy most directly supports learner autonomy?
options: Setting personal goals and monitoring progress
Waiting for the teacher to make every decision
questions.correctAnswer: Setting personal goals and monitoring progress
questions.explanation: Goal-setting and self-monitoring help learners take greater responsibility for learning.

questions.prompt: A learner uses flashcards with spaced review to remember vocabulary. Which characteristic is this?
questions.correctAnswer: Learning strategy
questions.explanation: The learner is using a deliberate technique to improve retention.

questions.prompt: Which behaviour shows a compensation strategy?
options: Paraphrasing when the exact word is unknown
Refusing to communicate until every word is known
Copying the date from the board
questions.correctAnswer: Paraphrasing when the exact word is unknown
questions.explanation: Paraphrasing helps a learner communicate despite a gap in language knowledge.

questions.prompt: Which statement about learning strategies is most accurate?
options: Different strategies may be useful for different tasks and learners
One strategy is best for every learner and task
Strategies are the same as learner needs
questions.correctAnswer: Different strategies may be useful for different tasks and learners
questions.explanation: Effective strategy use depends on the task, learner and learning goal.

questions.prompt: A learner decides to listen to English for ten minutes every day and records progress. What is most clearly demonstrated?
questions.correctAnswer: Goal-setting and self-monitoring
questions.explanation: The learner plans learning and tracks progress independently.

questions.prompt: Which teacher action best develops strategic competence as a learner?
options: Ask learners to reflect on which strategies helped and why
Prevent learners from evaluating their own work
questions.correctAnswer: Ask learners to reflect on which strategies helped and why
questions.explanation: Reflection helps learners become more aware of useful strategies and when to use them.

questions.prompt: A learner is used to grammar translation and feels uncomfortable when a new teacher uses pair work. Which characteristic is most relevant?
questions.correctAnswer: Past language-learning experience
questions.explanation: Previous classroom experience can shape expectations about what learning should look like.

questions.prompt: A learner previously failed a language course and now lacks confidence. Which factor may be influencing the learner?
questions.correctAnswer: Past learning experience
questions.explanation: Previous success or failure can affect confidence and expectations.

questions.prompt: Why should a teacher ask learners about previous language courses?
options: Past experiences may affect expectations, confidence and preferred classroom routines
It determines their CEFR level automatically
It eliminates the need for assessment
questions.correctAnswer: Past experiences may affect expectations, confidence and preferred classroom routines
questions.explanation: Previous learning can shape beliefs about teaching and learning.

questions.prompt: A learner expects the teacher to explain every grammar rule because that was normal in previous courses. What is this an example of?
questions.correctAnswer: Past learning experience influencing expectations
questions.explanation: Learners can develop strong beliefs about effective teaching from previous classrooms.

questions.prompt: How should a teacher respond when a new approach differs greatly from learners' previous experience?
options: Explain the purpose of the new approach and introduce it supportively
Assume resistance means learners are lazy
questions.correctAnswer: Explain the purpose of the new approach and introduce it supportively
questions.explanation: Making the rationale clear can help learners adapt to unfamiliar methods.

questions.prompt: A learner strongly prefers teacher correction because previous courses were highly teacher-centred. Which factor may explain this?
questions.correctAnswer: Past language-learning experience
questions.explanation: Previous teaching styles can shape expectations about teacher and learner roles.

questions.prompt: Which previous experience is most likely to reduce confidence?
options: Repeated unsuccessful attempts to learn a language
Successful completion of a challenging course
questions.correctAnswer: Repeated unsuccessful attempts to learn a language
questions.explanation: Past failure can influence present confidence and motivation.

questions.prompt: Which statement about past learning experience is most accurate?
options: It can affect how learners respond to a teacher's methods
It has no effect once a new course begins
questions.correctAnswer: It can affect how learners respond to a teacher's methods
questions.explanation: Prior experience influences expectations but does not determine all future learning.

questions.prompt: A class dislikes pair work because they have almost never used it before. What is a sensible first response?
options: Teach the routine gradually and explain its purpose
Conclude that pair work can never work with them
Force complex pair tasks immediately without support
questions.correctAnswer: Teach the routine gradually and explain its purpose
questions.explanation: Learners may need support to adapt to an unfamiliar classroom procedure.

questions.prompt: Which teacher question would best reveal relevant past learning experience?
options: What kinds of English classes and activities have you done before?
questions.correctAnswer: What kinds of English classes and activities have you done before?
questions.explanation: The question directly explores previous language-learning experiences.

questions.prompt: A learner needs English to give presentations at work. What type of need is this primarily?
questions.correctAnswer: Professional need
questions.explanation: The language is needed for present or future employment.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to pass an English-medium university course. Which type of need is especially relevant?
questions.correctAnswer: Learning/academic need
questions.explanation: The learner needs English to study successfully in an educational context.

questions.prompt: Which is an example of a personal learner need?
options: Wanting English to communicate while travelling
Needing to master a company's reporting format
Needing a specific exam score for university admission
questions.correctAnswer: Wanting English to communicate while travelling
questions.explanation: Personal needs can arise from individual interests, lifestyle and communication goals.

questions.prompt: Why is needs analysis useful?
options: It helps teachers choose relevant content, skills and priorities
It guarantees all learners want the same syllabus
questions.correctAnswer: It helps teachers choose relevant content, skills and priorities
questions.explanation: Understanding learner needs supports more purposeful course and lesson planning.

questions.prompt: A learner needs English for customer calls, has little study time and wants to become more independent. Which statement is best?
options: Needs can include professional goals, learning conditions and learner autonomy
Only the job goal counts as a need
Time availability is unrelated to learning
questions.correctAnswer: Needs can include professional goals, learning conditions and learner autonomy
questions.explanation: Learner needs can be personal, learning-related and professional, and can include practical constraints.

questions.prompt: Which learner most clearly has a future professional need?
options: A nursing student who will work in an English-speaking hospital
A learner who likes blue notebooks
questions.correctAnswer: A nursing student who will work in an English-speaking hospital
questions.explanation: The learner will need English for future employment.

questions.prompt: A learner has only 20 minutes a day available for independent study. Which category can this inform?
questions.correctAnswer: Learning needs
questions.explanation: Time availability affects how learning can realistically be organised.

questions.prompt: Which course decision best reflects learner needs?
options: Prioritise telephone language for learners who handle international calls
Teach identical content regardless of learners' goals
Choose topics only because the teacher likes them
questions.correctAnswer: Prioritise telephone language for learners who handle international calls
questions.explanation: Relevant language content should reflect learners' real communicative goals.

questions.prompt: Which question is most useful in a needs analysis?
options: What do you need to do in English now or in the future?
Which English letter do you like best?
questions.correctAnswer: What do you need to do in English now or in the future?
questions.explanation: The question identifies real personal, learning or professional purposes.

questions.prompt: Which statement about learner needs is most accurate?
options: Different learners in the same class may have different personal, learning and professional needs
All learners at the same level have identical needs
Needs are the same as learning preferences
questions.correctAnswer: Different learners in the same class may have different personal, learning and professional needs
questions.explanation: Language level alone does not determine why, what or how learners need to learn.

matchingSets.instruction: Match each learner description with the most relevant characteristic or need.

items.example: A teenager is very self-conscious about making mistakes in front of classmates.
A learner uses English daily at work but another only uses it in class.
A learner says diagrams help her understand new language.
A learner reviews vocabulary with spaced flashcards.
A learner expects grammar translation because previous courses used it.
A learner needs English to give presentations at work.

matchingSets.instruction: Match each example with the most relevant TKT concept.

items.example: Ability to manage longer abstract tasks develops with age.
An adult consciously analyses grammar rules.
A learner prefers collaborative discussion to individual reflection.
A learner sets a weekly goal and monitors progress.
Previous unsuccessful courses have reduced confidence.
A learner will need English for international customer calls.
